a statement on our Vision & Values
At The Heights Primary School we nurture the talents of individuals and celebrate their efforts and achievements.
Children are happy here. They feel safe, secure and able to express themselves. There is an exciting and energetic atmosphere at our school – it is a place full of positivity and opportunity.
Our KITE values are: Kind, Inquisitive, Thoughtful, Enthusiastic – Every Learner, Every Day.
take a look at our Key Statistics

Families think the school develops independence and responsibility

Attendance
Sickness
Attendance at The Heights Primary is vital for every child’s learning and wellbeing. Regular attendance helps pupils build strong routines, keep up with lessons, and make the most of teaching and support in class. When children are in school, they benefit not only from subject learning but also from friendships, confidence, and the wider opportunities that contribute to a positive school experience.
We ask parents and carers to work with us to ensure children attend every day they are able. If your child is unwell or there is another unavoidable reason for absence, please inform the school by phone or via the Arbor app as early as possible and provide any necessary details. Our team will monitor attendance patterns and, where appropriate, will offer support and guidance to help remove barriers to attendance and keep your child on track.
Exceptional circumstances
We strongly recommend that holidays are taken during half-term breaks or school holidays, as we do not authorise any holiday requests during term time. If you require time off for any reason during term time - such as a family emergency - you'll need to complete the absence report form below; a paper version can also be obtained from the school office.
Contacts
Any communication regarding attendance and absences should be sent via Arbor

The Heights Support Group is a friendly, welcoming support network, made up of our families with children with SEN, educational, emotional, physical or behavioural additional needs. Our group’s aim to to bring together these families for regular social meetings (with coffee and cakes!) to chat, moan, laugh or cry! And help support them through their children’s time with us. Admissions
Families do not pay fees at our school, as we are a state primary school.
When do I apply for a school place?
You must apply for a primary school place one year before your child can start school, when your child is three or has just turned four.
Applications are administered by Reading Borough Council and close on 15 January every year. Offer of places will be issued on 16 April 2027 for the September 2027 start.
Note: If you have siblings already enrolled at our school, you are still required to apply for a place.
How to apply
Families need to apply online through the Reading Borough Council website, Brighter Futures for Children. You'll need to create an account.
Our In-year transfers are managed by Brighter Futures for Children, and applications should be made directly to them. They will be able to advise if a place is available. Read more here.
Admissions Policy
Admissions Policy 2027-28.pdf
Waiting list
Unsuccessful applicants (including any late applications) will be included on the Reading Borough Council's waiting list, who manages them. Please note that our school has no control or influence over the management of the waiting list.
A child’s position on the waiting list can go down as well as up. For example, if a new application is received or if a child on the list moves nearer to the school, the waiting list will need to be revised. The offer of a place does not depend on the length of time your child’s name has been on the waiting list. Waiting lists will be held by the school for one school year after the year of entry.
Appeal
Our school is oversubscribed and not all applications will be successful. If you are not successful, you have the right to appeal with an independent panel. All appeals are managed by Reading Borough Council: you can read more and submit an appeal here.
Reading Council guide to admissions
For any queries relating to the admissions process, email admissions@theheightsprimary.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: The Heights Primary School - We are a Green School
pageCache.text:
We are a Green School
Our commitment to sustainability runs deep through every aspect of our school community. We recognise our responsibility to prepare our students not just for academic success, but for stewardship of our planet’s future.
Our Climate Action Plan
We have developed a comprehensive Climate Action Plan that sets ambitious but achievable goals for reducing our environmental impact. Key initiatives include:
Reading Climate Action Pledge
We are proud signatories of the Reading Climate Action Pledge, joining local businesses and community organizations in a collective commitment to combat climate change. Through this partnership, we:
Reading Climate Action Plan: The Heights Pledge
Share best practices with other local organizations
Participate in community-wide environmental initiatives
Report our progress transparently
Support student-led climate action projects
Collaborate with local businesses on sustainability initiatives
Our Achievements
Our dedication to sustainability has already yielded significant results:
Eco Council
Our pupils are at the heart of our sustainability journey. Our Eco Council meets regularly throughout the year to discuss and implement new environmental initiatives, while our Green Ambassador program enables children to lead sustainability projects across year groups.
A huge thank you to the amazing School and Eco Councillors, and also our School Ambassadors who work very hard in their roles.
Modeshift – Sustainable Travel
We are actively involved in the Modeshift Stars National Awards Scheme that has been established to recognise schools that have demonstrated excellence in supporting cycling, walking and other forms of sustainable travel. The scheme encourages schools across the country to join in a major effort to increase levels of sustainable and active travel in order to improve the health and well-being of children and young people. We are delighted to have achieved our Modeshift Gold Award for sustainable travel to and from school.
The Heights Primary School Travel Plan – April 2023
Looking forward
We continue to evolve our sustainability strategy, setting new targets and finding innovative ways to reduce our environmental impact. We invite all members of our school community—students, staff, parents, and local partners—to join us in this vital mission to create a more sustainable future.
To learn more about our sustainability initiatives or to get involved, contact our Sustainability Lead at anna.cahill@theheightsprimary.co.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Heights Primary School - Bellevue Place Education Trust
pageCache.text:
Bellevue Place Education Trust
The Bellevue Place Education Trust (BPET) is a multi-academy trust which supports primary schools across London and Berkshire, including The Heights Primary School.
What links all schools in the BPET family is the vision we are working towards: for every child to Learn, Enjoy, Succeed. All BPET schools have been judged by Ofsted to be 'Good', with four 'Outstanding'. Pupil achievement is high, driven by a broad and balanced curriculum. In addition, we offer 402 extra curricular activities every week, with 63% of pupils attending at least one club a week.
The Heights Primary School is state-funded and run on a not-for-profit basis. Parents do not pay fees to enrol children at our school.
LEARN
We offer a breadth and ambition of provision that supports an exceptional academic education, nurturing every child’s learning journey – regardless of ability, background or special educational needs – and helping them develop a lifelong passion for learning.
ENJOY
We believe learning should be enjoyable, and that through this enjoyment children develop life-long learning habits. We achieve this by creating opportunities for all children to reach their full potential at school, and to enjoy school life – helping to ensure pupils grow into happy, independent and confident learners.
SUCCEED
We strive for excellence, aiming to ignite ambition, aspiration, pride and a desire to contribute to society. We prepare our pupils to approach life with confidence, purpose and integrity.
Working together: the BPET way
We achieve far more by learning, supporting and collaborating within and across our network of schools and communities. We do so with an unwavering and shared commitment to equality, diversity, inclusion and respect.
Our family of schools
BPET family: Whitehall Park School, Braywick Court School, Kilburn Grange School, Halley House School, Deer Park School, Watling Park School, Evendons Primary School, Whiteknights Primary School, Rivermead Primary School, Dollis Primary School, Rutherford House School and The Heights Primary School.

Diversity & Inclusion
We are committed to ensuring equality of opportunity for all pupils, staff, parents, and carers. We actively promote fairness and respect, irrespective of race, gender, disability, belief, sexual orientation, age, or socio-economic background.
We strive to create and sustain a culture of inclusion, where every member of our school community feels valued, respected, and able to be proud of their identity. We believe that diversity strengthens our school, enriches our learning environment, and supports every child to thrive.
Guided by our values, we work collaboratively with families and the wider community to uphold an environment where differences are recognised, respected, and celebrated.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Heights Primary School - Trips and Residentials
pageCache.text:
Trips and Residentials
Educational trips and residentials provide safe opportunities for children to learn outside the classroom, develop important life skills, and they bring their classroom learning to life. These experiences are designed to complement the curriculum and enhance the children's learning in a fun and engaging way.
We understand the importance of caregivers and parental involvement in our trips and residentials, so we provide detailed information about each trip, including the itinerary, activities, and safety measures in place.
Day visits and internal workshops
Day visits and internal workshops are one of many ways for children to gain knowledge on topics taught in our curriculum, while engaging with their local community. We provide a range of activities to our pupils which enrich their learning.
Sustrans Big Walk and Wheel week
Diwali festival afternoon
Chinese New Year celebrations
Christmas productions and shows
Cultural and creative arts
Pizza making at Pizza Express
‘Seaside’ Perform workshops
Pancake workshop with professional baker
The Little Red Hen performance
Annual Year 6 production
Natural History Museum, Oxford
Ancient Egyptian day
Great Fire of London re-enactment
The Earth Trust Centre
Superstructures workshop with Master Builders
Mapledurham Playing Fields
Trips and visits
Residentials
In the Autumn term, Year 6 visits Skern Lodge Outdoor Activity Centre in Bideford, Devon, for a 5-day, 4-night residential experience. Skern Lodge offers a wide range of exciting outdoor and coastal activities, including high ropes, crabbing, bodyboarding, coastal traversing, kayaking, rafting, and archery, providing pupils with unforgettable adventures and team-building opportunities.
New for 2026, Year 4 will attend a 3-day, 2-night residential trip to Youlbury Action and Adventure Centre in rural Oxfordshire. Youlbury offers a fantastic range of outdoor activities, including a sensory trail, orienteering, shelter building, climbing incline, low ropes, abseiling, outdoor cooking, and campfires. This trip is the perfect opportunity for pupils to develop new skills, build confidence, and enjoy the experience of being away from home.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Heights Primary School - New Parents
pageCache.text:
New Parents
A very warm welcome to The Heights Primary School. We are delighted that you and your child are joining our school community, and we look forward to supporting your family throughout your child's educational journey.
Starting at a new school is an exciting milestone, and we understand that there can be lots of information to take in. To help make the transition as smooth as possible, we have created the New Parents Welcome Booklet.
This booklet has been designed as a helpful guide, bringing together all of the key information you may need before your child starts with us. Inside, you will find details about our school routines, communication methods, uniform expectations, attendance, lunches, wraparound care, clubs, important contacts, and answers to many frequently asked questions.
We hope that this booklet will provide reassurance, answer any initial queries, and help you feel confident and prepared for your child's first day at The Heights.
